questions.title: Usability and security (rewrite)
questions.stimulus: Rewrite from memory. Start with the real tension: security adds friction, and friction makes users work around it. Then give your ways and say how each keeps security while reducing friction.

parts.prompt: Explain the challenges of balancing usability with security in software design, and suggest ways developers can address these challenges.

marking_criteria.criterion:
Explains key challenges in balancing usability and security in software design

Suggests relevant and practical ways developers can address these challenges

Outlines challenges with some explanation

Suggests one or more ways developers can respond, with some relevance

Identifies basic challenges or general conflict between usability and security

Suggests a vague solution
Shows some understanding of usability or security in the context of software design

parts.sample_answer: Balancing usability with security is a challenge as enhancing one often compromises the other. An overly secure software might be cumbersome and difficult to use, which could deter users from adopting it. Conversely, enhancing usability might lead to vulnerabilities in security. Solutions include minimising user friction by streamlining authentication processes, implementing adaptive security measures that adjust based on user behaviour, and ensuring the security features are transparent but not overly intrusive. For example, developers can use straightforward notifications for security alerts to keep users informed without disrupting their experience. Additionally, providing secure defaults and ensuring that critical security settings are enabled by default can maintain a baseline of security.
